batch.readabilityReason: Required labels are legible, with strong primary card labels and smaller conditions/supporting explanations. No material clipping or overlap is visible. Compact seats have less hierarchical range but remain readable.
batch.consistencyReason: The same deep outer arches, accent inner arches, white label sheets, offset backing edges and thin connectors form a coherent family. Four-seat grid, horizontal progression, vertical handoff, wide parallel branches and portrait decision tree remain distinct and appropriate to their ratios.
batch.characterReason: Defining arch geometry, overlapping label strips, offset paper stacks and flat patterned construction are retained across every diagram. Losses are mostly level rectangular papers instead of the references’ independently tilted sheets, and mainly angular connectors instead of flowing merge curves. These reduce the loose assembled-paper character without erasing it.
retainedTraits: Pattern visible above and below overlapping white text strips
Offset gray backing sheets and edges
losses: Much less sheet rotation and irregular overlap
Mostly orthogonal or straight connector routing; fewer expressive curves
No dark rendition among the five allowed captures, so dark adaptation cannot be assessed

uncertainty.font: Raster appearance is compatible with the requested Japanese sans-serif and no missing glyph boxes are visible. Actual font family, fallback and font loading cannot be proved from PNGs; no font/source files were inspected.
uncertainty.scale: Captures are larger placement frames. Evaluation used original PNG pixels and the stated target artwork sizes (640x320, 360x240, 480x360, 720x240, 320x480); apparent artwork scale is compatible with a 1:1 inset, but CSS/device-pixel ratio and browser zoom were not independently verified.
uncertainty.exactLabelCodepoints: Required Japanese wording is visibly complete. Raster images cannot prove Unicode identity of visually equivalent colon glyphs or whitespace; line breaks and visual padding were normalized for label assessment.
